headline: METAL ENERGY CONFIRMS LARGE BC PORPHYRY AT NIV — Maiden drill hits copper-gold over 426m; 11 holes totaling 6,295m complete
snippet: Metal Energy's first-ever drill program at the NIV project in British Columbia confirmed a large porphyry copper-gold system in 11 holes totalling 6,295 metres on November 12, with copper and gold intersected across 426 metres and stronger results encountered in the northern portion of the target. The NIV discovery sits in British Columbia's Highland Valley corridor — Canada's largest copper-producing region — and the maiden program's success represents the first porphyry confirmation at a project where only geological and geophysical work existed before. The company's Highland Valley project has also commenced drilling in November, adding a second active BC copper target to the portfolio.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC SAVAL DRILLS 48.8M AT 4.24 G/T AU — Jerritt Canyon Nevada gold mine on course for H2 2027 restart
snippet: First Majestic Silver (NYSE/TSX: AG) reported positive exploration results at its Jerritt Canyon gold mine in Nevada on November 12, with drill hole SC-26-030 at the Saval target returning 48.8 metres at 4.24 g/t gold, including 19.8 metres at 7.39 g/t gold — results that significantly advance the case for a 2027 mine restart as underground development work and mill upgrades proceed. Jerritt Canyon was one of Nevada's largest gold producers in its operating years, and the high-grade Saval intercept is the clearest signal yet that the deposit holds the grades needed to support economic reactivation; a confirmed restart would add approximately 100,000 ounces of annual gold output to First Majestic's production base.

headline: GOLD SKIDS TO $3,942 AS CPI SHOCK SELLOFF HITS DAY 3 — Copper at $13,697/t as Fed rate-hike expectations cap all metals
snippet: SP Angel's Thursday November 12 morning market view opened with gold at US$3,942 per ounce — down sharply from $4,057 the previous session — as Monday's hotter-than-expected CPI data continues to ratchet Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations higher and pressure non-yielding assets. Copper traded at $13,697 per tonne, down from $13,840, with SMM flagging weak Chinese downstream demand as manufacturers defer purchases ahead of a December procurement cycle. The selloff is now three days running and covering multiple asset classes simultaneously — oil, equities and metals all lower — suggesting the CPI print triggered a broad positioning unwind that may need several more sessions to fully clear.

headline: ATALAYA POSTS RECORD Q3 COPPER AT RIOTINTO SPAIN — 13,967t production, €342M net cash; full-year guidance intact
snippet: Atalaya Mining (LSE/TSX: ATYM) reported record third-quarter earnings from its Riotinto copper mine in Spain, with Q3 2026 production reaching 13,967 tonnes of copper — up approximately 15% year-over-year and 3.5% above Q2 — alongside net cash of €342.1 million, one of the strongest balance sheets among mid-tier European copper producers. Ore grades averaged 0.40% copper at recoveries of 84.25%, both above the top of the 2026 guidance ranges, and management reiterated full-year production guidance while expressing optimism about meeting targets. The result positions Atalaya as a potential consolidator in an Iberian copper belt that is drawing renewed capital interest as European governments push to onshore critical mineral processing.

headline: GR SILVER DRILLS 35.45M AT 311 G/T AG IN SINALOA — SE Area spike hits 4,232 g/t; Parallel Breccia adds copper-tungsten
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) reported high-grade intercepts from its 20,000-metre step-out drill program at the Plomosas Project in Sinaloa, Mexico on November 11, led by 35.45 metres true width at 311 g/t silver in the SE Area including a 0.4-metre high-grade spike at 4,232 g/t silver. A second highlight hole in the Parallel Breccia Target returned 2.15 metres at 1,164 g/t silver alongside 0.6% copper and 0.37% tungsten — a polymetallic association that expands the project's economic potential beyond its silver base. The results extend the SE Area discovery zone further into previously untested ground at widths and grades that compare favourably to the company's existing resource, keeping Plomosas among the most active high-grade silver step-out campaigns on the TSX-V.

headline: WESTERN RIDGE DRILLS SHALLOW SILVER AT KEYSTONE NEVADA — 41m at 30.83 g/t Ag under historic mine, 7 more holes pending
snippet: Western Ridge Resources (ASX: WRX) reported that the first two drill holes at its Keystone project in Nevada intersected broad shallow silver zones directly beneath the outline of a historic silver mine — 41.15 metres at 30.83 g/t silver from 41.15 metres depth and 44.2 metres at 26.81 g/t silver from 30.48 metres — validating the geological model ahead of seven additional holes awaiting assay. The shallow, bulk-tonnage nature of the mineralisation at Keystone differs from most silver explorers currently active in Nevada, which target higher-grade underground systems; if remaining holes confirm grade consistency across the mineralised footprint, Western Ridge could be developing a low-strip-ratio open-pit silver resource in one of the world's most mining-friendly jurisdictions.

headline: MAGNA MINING Q3 PUTS ONTARIO NICKEL-COPPER ON TRACK — McCreedy West delivers 3.7M CuEq lbs; full-year 16-18M lb guidance holds
snippet: Magna Mining (TSX: NICU) reported Q3 2026 operating and financial results on November 11 showing 3.7 million copper-equivalent payable pounds produced from its McCreedy West mine in Sudbury, Ontario, with the company maintaining its full-year 2026 guidance of 16–18 million CuEq payable pounds. McCreedy West is one of the few producing base-metal mines in Sudbury's copper-nickel belt to have ramped up under current management, and Magna is separately evaluating a potential restart of the Intermediate nickel zone — a decision that would add nickel production to what is currently a copper-dominant output profile at a time when nickel prices have been depressed by Indonesian oversupply.

headline: CENTENARIO GOLD DRILLS COPPER-GOLD SKARN AT LOS REYES CHIHUAHUA — Copper oxides confirmed, mineralization extends at depth
snippet: Centenario Gold reported on November 12 that its Los Reyes copper-gold skarn project in Chihuahua, Mexico confirmed copper oxide intercepts in an initial five-hole, 1,140-metre drill program, with vertical mineralisation extending below the Jibosa-Tueda Zone where previous surface sampling had identified copper-gold grades. Skarn systems in Chihuahua have historically produced some of North America's most economically robust copper-gold mines due to high-grade mineralisation where pyrrhotite and magnetite alteration is strongest; if deeper holes confirm the vertical extent suggested by these initial intercepts, Los Reyes could develop into a significant underground copper-gold target in a proven Mexican mining jurisdiction.

headline: SUN SUMMIT MAPS 12KM PORPHYRY TREND AT BUCK BC — Only 2 of multiple targets drilled; 3 large IP anomalies define district upside
snippet: Sun Summit Minerals (TSX-V: SUMS) identified a 12.0-kilometre trend of porphyry copper-gold targets at its Buck Project in British Columbia after summer 2026 exploration defined three large induced polarization anomalies along the CR Porphyry Trend, with only two of the multiple targets tested by drilling to date. The 12-kilometre scale puts Buck in the same size class as known BC porphyry districts — a footprint that would justify multi-year systematic testing — and the low number of holes drilled against the IP-defined target area means a single strong intersection could re-rate the company significantly against its current exploration-stage market cap.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER TESTS ANDESITE BRECCIA AT KWANIKA — Step-out confirms expansion potential beyond high-grade Western Zone, BC
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSX-V: NWST) reported exploration-target drill results highlighting expansion potential at the Andesite Breccia zone adjacent to the established Kwanika copper-gold porphyry in central British Columbia, with 14 of 43 holes from the 2026 program now reported. The Andesite Breccia target sits outside the economic envelope modelled in the preliminary feasibility study, so positive results there expand resource inventory without cannibalising the base case; Kwanika already hosts 1.4 billion pounds of copper and 2.4 million ounces of gold, making any meaningful addition at adjacent targets disproportionately valuable to project economics and to the case for a Tier-1 BC copper development decision.
